column1: # gpu-probe TRADITIONAL ladder - the industry-standard stress tools, one per step.
# Same harness, same telemetry, same verdicts as steps/xid79.tsv, so a PASS here
# means the same thing it meant there.  NO Folding@home anywhere in this table:
# it exists to answer 'is the card sick, or is this box sick?' with tools whose
# behaviour is well known - if the standard suite is clean and only folding kills
# it, the fault is in the folding path, not in the silicon.
# 'requires' is checked with command -v: a missing tool is SKIP-TOOL, not a result.
# Run it through the bundle that provides the tools, e.g.
# GL steps need the console session: arm.sh passes DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY through.

column4: OpenGL raster/composite: the FurMark class of test, on this card's own console output
sustained fragment-shader fill at native console resolution: max clocks, no memory traffic
GPU VRAM + copy path at ~150 GB/s with data verification (the traditional memtest-of-vram)
OpenCL bandwidth + FP32/FP64 kernels through the vendor ICD, on the GPU device
full OpenCL kernel sweep with an honest budget (the 330 s run was cut mid-benchmark, card alive)
CPU: every ALU/FPU method in turn, each result verified by stress-ng itself
memory subsystem: 2 writers hammering 2 GiB, page + DRAM traffic
RAM + cache with data verification (Google); -M 1536 MiB on a 7.7 GiB box
classic userspace RAM pattern march over 1 GiB of live memory
independent CPU implementation to cross-check stress-ng
combined load: 8 CPU threads while the GPU verifies its VRAM (the classic PSU/VRM test)
re-run the most sensitive GPU probe last: healthy-before AND healthy-after is the proof
